# Archive, reclone and delete a workspace

## Intent

The owner of a repository workspace can retire it, revive it, repair its copy and finally remove it. Archiving takes the workspace out of service without losing anything the hub holds; reactivating brings it back; recloning throws the hub's copy away and fetches origin again; deleting removes an archived workspace, its task forks and everything they own in one step or not at all. Each of these offers the hub's branches to origin first where commits could otherwise be lost, and none of them leaves a workspace half changed.

## Goals

- `POST /workspaces/:slug/archive` on a `ready` or `failed` repository workspace answers `200` with `status: "archived"`, keeps the hub's copy, and emits `parley.workspace.archive` with `head_sha`, `origin_push` and the number of forks.
- Before archiving and before recloning, the hub offers every branch to origin as a fast-forward; whatever origin answers, the operation goes on, and the event says `origin_push: ok`, `partial` or `failed`.
- Archive ends every active agent session of the workspace and of its forks with reason `workspace archived`; a failure to end one does not fail the archive.
- `POST /workspaces/:slug/reactivate` on an `archived` workspace answers `200` with `status: "pending"`, and clone work brings it back to `ready` from the kept copy.
- `POST /workspaces/:slug/reclone` on a `ready` or `failed` repository workspace without forks answers `200` with `status: "pending"`, `sync_error: null` and `origin_head_sha: null`; the new copy holds what origin holds and nothing else.
- `DELETE /workspaces/:slug` on an `archived` repository workspace answers `204`; afterwards the workspace, its forks, the tokens bound to them and everything they own are gone, the slug can be registered again, and one `parley.workspace.delete` exists for each fork and one for the parent. When the removal fails the answer is `500` and nothing has changed.
- While one of archive, reclone and delete runs on a workspace, every other request that needs its repository answers `409 workspace_busy`.
- `parley workspace archive|reactivate|reclone|delete` drive the four routes; `reclone` and `delete` send nothing without `--confirm`.

## Background

The repository holds no code yet; every file named here is new. Source: `docs/prd/04_workspaces_and_forks.md`, WS-FR-058 to WS-FR-065 with the rows of §4.3.4 for archive, reactivate, reclone and delete, the four routes of §4.5, the four commands of §4.6, the four events of §4.8 and the edge cases of §4.10 that name archive and reactivate. WS-FR-080 (one delete event for each fork) is described under WS-FR-065 and is covered here for the delete of a parent.

Package 10 workspace_create_and_clone delivers the workspace record, the state guard with the read side of the maintenance marker, clone work (a workspace in `pending` is its own clone work), credential resolution from workspace secrets, and in `internal/gitrepo/` the operations to open and to remove a copy. This package adds to `internal/workspace/`: the maintenance marker's set and release side (`maintenance.go`), the safety copy (`safetycopy.go`), the collaborators other packages supply (`teardown.go`), and one file for each operation with its handler (`archive.go`, `reactivate.go`, `reclone.go`, `delete.go`), each with its test file beside it. It adds to `internal/gitrepo/` the push of many branches to a remote as fast-forwards (`pushall.go`), and to `internal/cli/workspace.go` the commands `archive`, `reactivate`, `reclone` and `delete`. An end-to-end test in `test/e2e/workspace_retire_test.go` starts a real hub in-process and drives it over HTTP, through the CLI and against a test origin.

## Requirements

All paths are relative to `/api/v1`. Errors are the error envelope of the platform conventions; "`409 has_forks`" means HTTP 409 with `error_type` `has_forks`. The four routes take no body and need the scope `workspaces:write` and write access: the owner and the admin token may call them; a member of the organization gets `403 forbidden`, also on an archived workspace; a caller without access gets `404 not_found`, the same answer as for an unknown slug.

### Exclusive maintenance (§4.3.4, WS-FR-007)

Archive, reclone and delete each put the workspace in exclusive maintenance for the length of the call: the maintenance marker is set after the checks have passed and released when the call ends, whether it succeeded or failed. While the marker is set, a second archive, reactivate, reclone or delete of the same workspace answers `409 workspace_busy`, and so does every route that asks package 10's state guard. Of two concurrent calls on one workspace, exactly one runs and the other answers `409 workspace_busy`. Workspaces do not block each other.

Once the checks have passed, each of the three operations runs to its end when the caller disconnects.

### The safety copy to origin (WS-FR-058, WS-FR-063)

Before an archive and before a reclone the hub offers every branch under `refs/heads/` of its copy to the branch of the same name on origin, with the origin credential resolved from the workspace's secrets. The offer is fast-forward only: it never forces, never deletes a branch on origin and sends no tags. On a carry-patch workspace the integration branch is left out, because the hub rebuilds it; patch branches are offered.

The outcome is one of three values and goes into the event of the operation:

| `origin_push` | Condition |
|---|---|
| `ok` | origin accepted every offered branch (a branch origin already had at that commit counts as accepted), or there was no branch to offer |
| `partial` | origin accepted at least one branch and refused at least one |
| `failed` | origin accepted none of at least one offered branch: every branch was refused, origin could not be reached, the credential was refused or could not be read, or the 2-minute deadline passed before any branch was accepted |

The outcome never changes what the operation does or answers. For every branch origin accepted, the hub records the pushed commit as the origin head of that branch, the ref `refs/remotes/origin/<name>` of its copy. The safety copy has a deadline of 2 minutes; branches not accepted by then count as refused. No credential and no text from origin appears in a response or an event.

### Archive (WS-FR-058 to WS-FR-061)

`POST /workspaces/:slug/archive` applies to a repository workspace in `ready` or `failed`. The first row that applies decides:

| Workspace | Answer |
|---|---|
| a fork | `400 not_supported_on_fork` |
| the maintenance marker is set | `409 workspace_busy` |
| `archived` | `409 workspace_archived` |
| `pending` or `cloning` | `409 workspace_busy` |

On a workspace that passes, the hub makes the safety copy (a `failed` workspace has no copy, so nothing is offered), then in one transaction sets `status: "archived"`, clears `clone_error`, and writes `parley.workspace.archive`. The answer is `200` with the workspace object, `status: "archived"`.

The hub's copy of the repository is not touched: every branch, every ref under `refs/parley/` and every change version it held before the archive is still in it afterwards. Bound tokens, secrets, variables, patches, changes and forks are not touched. An archived workspace is still read with `GET /workspaces/:slug`.

The event `parley.workspace.archive` has the caller as actor, the slug as `workspace`, and metadata `head_sha` (the workspace's `head_sha`, `null` when it has none), `origin_push` and `forks` (the number of forks the workspace has). A refused archive emits no event.

**Sessions.** Inside the archive's transaction the hub asks the session closer to end every active agent session of the workspace and of each of its forks with reason `workspace archived`. When the closer fails, its own writes are undone and the archive still commits and answers `200`.

**Observers.** After the transaction has committed the hub tells each archive observer the slug and the slugs of its forks (package 47 stops sandboxes this way). An observer's failure is logged and changes nothing in the answer.

### Reactivate (WS-FR-062)

`POST /workspaces/:slug/reactivate` applies to an `archived` repository workspace. The first row that applies decides:

| Workspace | Answer |
|---|---|
| a fork | `400 not_supported_on_fork` |
| the maintenance marker is set | `409 workspace_busy` |
| any status other than `archived` | `409 workspace_not_archived` |

On an archived workspace the hub, in one transaction, sets `status: "pending"`, clears `clone_error` and writes `parley.workspace.reactivate` (caller as actor, no metadata); it then wakes the clone workers through package 10's entry point. The answer is `200` with the workspace object, `status: "pending"`. Clone work finds the kept copy and the workspace becomes `ready` without a clone; when the copy is damaged or missing it is cloned fresh from origin, and commits that existed only in the hub are gone (package 10, WS-FR-026).

### Reclone (WS-FR-063)

`POST /workspaces/:slug/reclone` applies to a repository workspace in `ready` or `failed`, checked in this order:

| Workspace | Answer |
|---|---|
| a fork | `400 fork_has_no_origin` |
| the maintenance marker is set | `409 workspace_busy` |
| `archived` | `409 workspace_archived` |
| `pending` or `cloning` | `409 workspace_busy` |
| has at least one fork | `409 has_forks` |

On a workspace that passes, the hub makes the safety copy, then in one transaction sets `status: "pending"`, clears `sync_error` and `origin_head_sha`, marks the existing copy as not belonging to the record any more, and writes `parley.workspace.reclone` with metadata `origin_push`. It then discards the copy on disk, and with it the origin head of every branch (the refs `refs/remotes/origin/<name>`), and wakes the clone workers. The answer is `200` with the workspace object: `status: "pending"`, `sync_error: null`, `origin_head_sha: null`.

When the transaction fails the answer is `500 internal`, the status and the copy are as before, and no event exists. After the clone that follows, the copy holds exactly origin's branches and tags: a branch that existed only in the hub and was not accepted by origin is gone, and so is every ref under `refs/parley/`. Change records are not removed.

### Delete (WS-FR-064, WS-FR-065, WS-FR-080)

`DELETE /workspaces/:slug` on a repository workspace applies only when it is `archived`. The first row that applies decides:

| Workspace | Answer |
|---|---|
| a fork | handed to `DeleteFork` of the fork remover that package 16 registers; `500 internal` when none is registered |
| the maintenance marker is set | `409 workspace_busy` |
| a repository workspace in any status other than `archived` | `409 workspace_not_archived` |

The delete of an archived repository workspace W with forks F1…Fn runs in three stages.

1. **Sandboxes.** The hub asks the sandbox remover to delete the sandboxes of W and of every fork. When it fails the answer is `500 internal` and no workspace record, token or other data has changed.
2. **The removal step, one transaction.** For each fork and then for W, the hub revokes the live tokens bound to the slug through the token revoker, runs every registered remover of owned data (workspace secrets and variables, patches, changes, policy, claims, workspace sandbox rules and event webhook subscriptions with their undelivered events are removed), asks the session closer to end the remaining active sessions with reason `workspace deleted`, removes the workspace record with its settings, and writes one `parley.workspace.delete` event. When any part fails, the whole transaction is rolled back, the answer is `500 internal`, and nothing has changed: W is still `archived`, its forks exist, no token is revoked, no event was written.
3. **Repository data.** Only after the transaction has committed does the hub discard the repository data of W, which holds the branches of its forks. A failure here is logged; the answer is still `204`, and the leftover is never taken for the copy of a later workspace with the same slug (package 10).

The answer is `204` with an empty body. Afterwards `GET /workspaces/<slug>` answers `404 not_found` for W and for each fork, and `POST /workspaces` with W's slug succeeds. Audit records and the event log are kept.

Each `parley.workspace.delete` event has the caller as actor, the deleted slug as `workspace`, and metadata `kind` (`repository` or `fork`), `parent_slug` (`null` for W), `revoked_tokens` (the ids of the tokens that were bound to that workspace and were revoked by this step, sorted ascending, `[]` when none) and, on W's event only, `deleted_forks` (the fork slugs, sorted ascending, `[]` when none).

### CLI (§4.6)

The commands follow the CLI's common rules: the route's response on stdout as one JSON document, a hub error on stderr with exit 1, a usage error with exit 2.

| Command | Request | Flags | Request timeout | stdout |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `parley workspace archive <slug>` | `POST /workspaces/:slug/archive` | none | 3 minutes | the workspace |
| `parley workspace reactivate <slug>` | `POST /workspaces/:slug/reactivate` | `--wait`, `--timeout`, `--poll-interval` | 30 seconds | the workspace |
| `parley workspace reclone <slug>` | `POST /workspaces/:slug/reclone` | `--confirm` (required), `--wait`, `--timeout`, `--poll-interval` | 3 minutes | the workspace |
| `parley workspace delete <slug>` | `DELETE /workspaces/:slug` | `--confirm` (required) | 30 seconds | `{"status": "deleted", "slug": "<slug>"}` |

`reclone` and `delete` without `--confirm` exit 2 with a `usage_error` on stderr and send no request. With `--wait`, `reactivate` and `reclone` poll `GET /workspaces/:slug` after the `200` as `parley workspace create` does: `ready` prints the final workspace and exits 0; `failed` prints the final workspace, reports `wait_failed` on stderr and exits 1. The slug is sent as one percent-encoded path segment.

### End-to-end flows

1. **Retire and revive.** A developer runs `parley workspace archive demo`; the CLI posts to the hub; `parleyd` offers the branches to origin, archives the workspace and answers `200`; origin now has the commit that existed only in the hub; the developer runs `parley workspace reactivate demo --wait`; `parleyd` sets `pending`, the clone work finds the kept copy, and the command prints the workspace with `status: "ready"` and the same `head_sha` as before the archive.
2. **Delete with forks.** A developer archives a workspace that has a fork and a token bound to the fork, then runs `parley workspace delete demo --confirm`; `parleyd` removes the fork and the workspace in one step and discards the repository data; the command prints `{"status": "deleted", "slug": "demo"}`; two `parley.workspace.delete` events exist; the developer registers `demo` again and gets `201`.
3. **Reclone.** A developer runs `parley workspace reclone demo --confirm --wait` on a workspace that has one branch origin refuses; `parleyd` offers the branches, discards its copy, sets `pending` and clones origin; the command prints the workspace with `status: "ready"`; the refused branch is not in the new copy.

## Design Decisions

1. **Stack (project-wide).** Go; the hub runs the `git` command (2.38 or later) as a subprocess through `internal/gitrepo`, with no git library; HTTP on the standard library `net/http` router; the store is embedded SQLite through `modernc.org/sqlite` behind `internal/store`; the CLI uses `github.com/spf13/cobra`; tests use `testing` with tables and `net/http/httptest`, and repositories made with `git init` in `t.TempDir()`.
2. **Other packages' data is removed through collaborators.** Delete must revoke tokens, close sessions, delete sandboxes and remove data of more than ten other packages, most of them built later. `internal/workspace/teardown.go` therefore defines one collaborator set (`Teardown`) that the hub's composition fills at start, in `internal/hub/workspace.go` for this package's own entries and in each owner's `internal/hub/<area>.go` for the others (package 03 owns process composition in `internal/hub`; nothing is wired in `cmd/parleyd`): a `SandboxRemover` (called before the removal step), a `TokenRevoker` (called inside the removal transaction; it returns the ids of the tokens it revoked), `Remover`s of owned data (called inside the removal transaction with one slug; they return an error only), a `SessionCloser` (called inside the archive and the removal transaction with a reason), `ArchiveObserver`s (called after an archive committed) and a `ForkRemover`. With none registered the operations still work and touch only the workspace records. Why: it keeps the plan's dependencies and makes "one step or nothing" a property of one transaction. This package wires, in `internal/hub/workspace.go`, what its own dependencies provide: `RevokeBoundTo` of package 08 as the token revoker (tokens have no remover of their own) and `secret.RemoveWorkspace(tx, slug)` of package 39 as a remover of owned data. Package 39 cannot depend on this package, so it only exports the function and this package registers it; this package reaches package 39 through package 10. Every other owner registers itself in `Teardown` from its own `internal/hub/<area>.go`. The removers of owned data are: secrets (39, registered here), variables (40), forge deliveries (43), event webhooks (53), sessions (49), sandboxes and sandbox rules (47, 48), changes (22), policy (27), claims (30), and patches, jobs and rerere records (31, 33, 34). Package 47 also registers the sandbox remover and an archive observer (which stops sandboxes), package 49 the session closer and package 16 the fork remover.
3. **Forks: one interface, implemented by package 16.** This package registers `DELETE /workspaces/:slug` for both kinds and declares `ForkRemover` with two methods. `DeleteFork` serves the route for a fork slug; until a fork remover is registered the route answers `500 internal` for a fork. `RemoveForksOf` removes the forks of a workspace inside this package's removal transaction, writes their events and returns their slugs and a function that discards their repository data after the commit. Fork removal thus has one place, package 16, once that package is built; while no fork remover is registered this package removes fork records by the same per-workspace removal it applies to the workspace, so that it can be built and tested without package 16. One registry serves both packages: `RemoveOwned` (token revoker, removers of owned data, session closer) is exported here and package 16 removes a fork's owned data through it, by request, by expiry and with its parent, and keeps no registry of its own. Why: one route serves both kinds, fork deletion has its own rules (WS-FR-078), and a package that stores data per workspace registers one remover and is called for every way a workspace or a fork goes away.
4. **The maintenance marker lives in memory.** It is a per-slug entry in the `parleyd` process, set after the checks and released when the call ends. A hub that stops in the middle of a call starts with no marker. Why: the hub is one process, and each operation changes the store in one transaction, so there is no half-done state to guard after a restart.
5. **Order of the refusals.** Fork first (`400`), then the maintenance marker (`409 workspace_busy`, as package 10's guard checks the marker first), then the status (`409`), then `has_forks`. Reactivate and delete answer `409 workspace_not_archived` for every status other than `archived`, including `pending` and `cloning`; `409 workspace_busy` is answered by them only while the marker is set. Why: the PRD lists `workspace_busy` and `workspace_not_archived` for these routes without an order; the check order of the platform puts validation before state.
6. **Meaning of `origin_push`.** The PRD names the three values and not their conditions; the table under "The safety copy to origin" defines them. No branch to offer is `ok`, because nothing was refused.
7. **The safety copy has one 2-minute deadline for all branches.** The PRD gives none; 2 minutes is the push-to-origin deadline (WS-FR-054), and the CLI's 3-minute timeout for archive and reclone then always receives the hub's answer.
8. **The safety copy records origin heads (the refs `refs/remotes/origin/<name>`, through `SetOriginHead` of `internal/gitrepo`) and emits no `parley.workspace.push`.** WS-FR-056 counts pushes of the push route; the outcome of the safety copy is in the archive or reclone event. Recording the accepted heads keeps a later forced push's lease truthful.
9. **Archive commits even when the session closer fails.** WS-FR-060 says a failure to close a session does not fail the archive; AUD-FR-009 puts the closing in the workspace's transaction. The closer runs inside the archive's transaction under a savepoint: its failure undoes only its own writes.
10. **Reclone is safe against a crash.** The transaction that sets `pending` also replaces the record's instance id (package 10, decision 4), so a copy that survives a crash between the commit and the discard is not valid for the record and is cloned fresh. `head_sha`, `default_branch` and `last_sync_at` are left as they are until the clone completes; the PRD names only the fields that are cleared.
11. **The three operations run to completion when the caller disconnects.** The PRD says so for sync and push; an archive or delete that stopped half-way at a closed connection would leave the caller unable to know the state.
12. **A failing sandbox remover stops the delete with `500 internal`.** The PRD says sandboxes are deleted first and nothing about a failure. Sandboxes that were already deleted stay deleted; no workspace data has changed, and the delete can be repeated.
13. **A failure to discard repository data after the removal committed is logged, and the answer stays `204`.** The workspace no longer exists; a `500` would say nothing was deleted.
14. **A body sent to the four routes is ignored** once it passes the platform's content-type and size rules; the PRD says "No body".
15. **`--wait` polls `GET /workspaces/:slug`,** which package 11 delivers, as `parley workspace create --wait` does (package 10, decision 15); package 11 is a dependency.
16. **`deleted_forks` and the fork events are ordered by slug ascending;** the parent's event is written last.

17. **Origin heads are refs.** They are `refs/remotes/origin/<name>` of the copy (packages 10 and 12), not rows. A reclone therefore clears them by discarding the copy, and a delete removes them with the repository data; the transaction clears only `origin_head_sha`.
18. **One test origin.** The safety copy is tested against `internal/gitrepo/gitrepotest` of package 10 in the push mode package 13 adds; this package adds no helper and no mode.

## Glossary

- **Hub**: The `parleyd` server.
- **Workspace**: A repository the hub holds, identified by its `slug`. Either a registered repository or a task fork.
- **Origin**: A registered workspace's remote (`git_url`).
- **Task fork (fork)**: A workspace created from another workspace (its parent) for one task. It shares history with the parent, has its own branches and expires: after 7 days by default, or 24 hours after all its changes have landed or been abandoned.
- **Carry-patch workspace**: A workspace that tracks an upstream project and keeps an ordered list of patches on top of it.
- **Integration branch**: For a carry-patch workspace, the branch the hub rebuilds as upstream plus the ordered patches.
- **Bound token**: A PAT confined to one workspace (and the forks created with it). A token bound to a fork also reaches its own changes, and the awareness and policy reads, on the fork's parent (§3).
- **Sandbox**: An isolated environment in which an agent runs, attached to a workspace (normally a task fork) and started with it checked out. It runs on OpenShell; the hub controls it (§13).
- **Session**: An agent session: who ran, on which workspace, with what token usage, and which changes it produced.
- **Hub event**: A record of something the hub did (`parley.*` types), with a sequence number. Hub events form the audit log and the event stream.
- **Origin head**: For a branch of a repository workspace, the last head the hub saw on origin.
- **Clone work**: The durable instruction to make or re-check the hub's copy of a workspace; a workspace in `pending` or `cloning` has clone work outstanding.
- **Maintenance marker**: The record that a reclone, archive or delete is running on a workspace.
- **Safety copy**: The fast-forward offer of every branch to origin that the hub makes before an archive and before a reclone.

# Requirements

## Requirements

### REQ-1: Exclusive maintenance and the rules the four routes share

**Rationale:** An archive, a reclone and a delete each change a whole workspace; a second one running beside it, or a caller without write access, must never leave it half changed.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-1.1] WHILE an archive, reclone or delete call is running on a workspace, THE parleyd SHALL answer every further archive, reactivate, reclone and delete request for that workspace with a busy refusal and make the state guard of other routes report the workspace as busy
   → HTTP 409 with error_type workspace_busy; the workspace record, its copy and the event log are unchanged by the refused request
   Check: unit
   - setup: a store with repository workspaces 'demo' and 'other'
   - setup: stub collaborators that record their calls

   ```
1. [REQ-1.2] WHEN an archive, reclone or delete call ends, by success, by a refusal after the marker was set, or by a failure, THE parleyd SHALL release the maintenance marker of that workspace
   → after the call has answered, the marker is not set and the next request for the workspace is judged by its status alone

   ```

   → one call answers its success status, the other HTTP 409 with error_type workspace_busy; exactly one event of the operation exists for the workspace
   Check: integration

### REQ-2: Safety copy to origin

**Rationale:** Commits that exist only in the hub should reach origin before the hub stops serving or discards them, yet origin must never be able to block the owner.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-2.1] WHEN an archive or a reclone has passed its checks on a workspace whose copy exists, THE parleyd SHALL offer every branch under refs/heads/ of the hub's copy to the branch of the same name on origin as a fast-forward, with the origin credential resolved from the workspace's secrets, sending no tag, forcing nothing and deleting nothing on origin, and record the pushed commit as the origin head of every branch origin accepted, by setting the ref refs/remotes/origin/<name> of the hub's copy
   → after the offer origin holds every accepted branch at the hub's commit, no branch of origin was rewound or deleted, origin has no new tag, and the ref refs/remotes/origin/<name> of the hub's copy resolves to the pushed commit for each accepted branch
   Check: integration
   - setup: a test origin of internal/gitrepo/gitrepotest in its push mode (SmartOrigin, added by package 13) that requires Basic authentication and holds branches main, stale and old
   - setup: a hub copy cloned from it in which main is two commits ahead, a branch feat and a tag v-hub exist only in the hub, branch old was deleted, and stale was rewritten so that it is not a descendant of origin's stale
   - setup: the workspace secret GIT_PAT holds the token origin accepts
   ```
   in internal/workspace/safetycopy_test.go with a real git subprocess: run the safety copy; assert origin main == hub main, origin has feat at the hub's commit, origin stale still exists at its old commit, origin old still exists although the hub has no such branch, origin has no tag v-hub; assert refs/remotes/origin/main and refs/remotes/origin/feat of the hub's copy equal the pushed commits and refs/remotes/origin/stale is unchanged; assert the request origin received carried Basic authentication for user x-token-auth; assert the outcome is partial
   ```
1. [REQ-2.2] WHERE the workspace's workspace_mode is carry_patch, THE parleyd SHALL leave the integration branch out of the offer and offer the branches of patches like any other branch
   → origin's integration branch is unchanged; every other branch is offered
   Check: integration
   - setup: a carry-patch workspace whose integration_branch is 'deploy'
   - setup: in the hub copy both deploy and patch/a are ahead of origin

[REQ-2.3] THE parleyd SHALL for any safety copy, report exactly one outcome: ok when origin accepted every offered branch or there was no branch to offer, partial when origin accepted at least one branch and refused at least one, failed when at least one branch was offered and origin accepted none

### REQ-7: Transactional removal of a workspace, its forks and what they own

**Rationale:** A delete that stops half-way would leave live tokens for a workspace that no longer exists, or a workspace without its policy; one step or nothing rules that out.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-7.1] WHEN a delete of an archived repository workspace has passed its checks, THE parleyd SHALL ask the sandbox remover to delete the sandboxes of the workspace and of every fork of it before any record is changed
   → the sandbox remover is called once with the slugs of the workspace and of all its forks, before the removal transaction begins
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/workspace/delete_test.go: DELETE 'demo' with forks 'demo--a', 'demo--b' and a stub sandbox remover that reads the store when called; assert it was called once with the slugs {'demo', 'demo--a', 'demo--b'}; assert at that moment all three workspace rows existed and no remover of owned data had been called
   ```
1. [REQ-7.2] IF the sandbox remover returns an error, THEN THE parleyd SHALL stop the delete, answer with an internal error and change no workspace record, token or other owned data
   → HTTP 500 with error_type internal; workspace still archived; forks, tokens, owned data, copy and event log unchanged; a repeated delete can succeed
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/workspace/delete_test.go: the stub sandbox remover returns an error; DELETE 'demo'; assert r.status == 500 and error.error_type == 'internal'; assert the rows of 'demo' and its forks are unchanged with 'demo' archived; assert no remover and no session closer was called; assert the copy exists and no parley.workspace.delete event exists; then make the remover succeed and DELETE again: assert 204
   ```
1. [REQ-7.3] WHEN the sandboxes of an archived repository workspace under deletion have been deleted, THE parleyd SHALL in one transaction remove first the forks and then the workspace. The forks are removed by RemoveForksOf of the registered fork remover, called once with the transaction, the workspace's slug and the caller; when no fork remover is registered each fork, in ascending slug order, is removed by the same per-workspace removal as the workspace. The per-workspace removal revokes the live tokens bound to the slug through the token revoker, runs every registered remover of owned data with the slug, asks the session closer to end the remaining active sessions of the slug with the reason workspace deleted, and removes the workspace record with its settings
   → without a fork remover: the token revoker, every registered remover and the session closer (reason "workspace deleted") are called once for each removed workspace; with a fork remover: RemoveForksOf is called once and the revoker, the removers and the closer are called by this package for the workspace's own slug only; every call receives the transaction that removes the workspace records, and nothing is visible to other readers before the commit
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/workspace/delete_test.go: register a stub token revoker and two stub removers (secrets, changes) that each delete their own test rows keyed by slug through the transaction they are given, and a stub session closer; DELETE 'demo' with forks 'demo--b', 'demo--a'; assert the revoker and each remover were called exactly three times with slugs in the order 'demo--a', 'demo--b', 'demo'; assert the closer was called with those three slugs and reason 'workspace deleted'; assert every call received the same transaction; assert the removers' test rows and the three workspace rows are gone after the commit and were still visible to a second connection before it. Then register also a stub fork remover whose RemoveForksOf deletes the two fork rows through the transaction and returns ['demo--a', 'demo--b'] with a discard function: DELETE 'demo'; assert RemoveForksOf was called once with the same transaction, 'demo' and the caller; assert the revoker, the removers and the closer were called by this package once each, with 'demo' only; assert the discard function was called once, after the commit
   ```
1. [REQ-7.4] IF the token revoker, a remover of owned data, the fork remover, the session closer, the removal of a record or the write of an event fails inside the removal step, THEN THE parleyd SHALL roll the whole transaction back, answer with an internal error, and discard no repository data
   → HTTP 500 with error_type internal; the workspace is still archived, every fork exists, no token is revoked, no owned data is removed, no delete event is stored, and the repository data is intact
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/workspace/delete_test.go, table over the part made to fail {first remover on the first fork; last remover on the parent; the token revoker; RemoveForksOf of a registered stub fork remover, whose discard function must then not run; the session closer; removal of the parent's record; the write of the parent's event}: DELETE 'demo' with two forks; assert r.status == 500 and error.error_type == 'internal'; assert all three workspace rows exist and 'demo' is archived; assert the test rows of removers that ran before the failure exist again; assert no parley.workspace.delete event exists; assert the copy directory exists; assert the marker is released
   ```
1. [REQ-7.5] WHEN the removal step of a delete commits, THE parleyd SHALL write, in the removal transaction, one event parley.workspace.delete for each fork and one for the workspace, the workspace's last, each with the caller as actor, the deleted slug as workspace and the metadata kind, parent_slug and revoked_tokens (the ids the token revoker returned for that slug), and on the workspace's event also deleted_forks; when a fork remover is registered it writes the forks' events inside RemoveForksOf and this package writes the workspace's event with the slugs RemoveForksOf returned as deleted_forks
   → for a workspace with n forks, n+1 parley.workspace.delete events: fork events carry {kind: "fork", parent_slug: string, revoked_tokens: sorted string array}; the workspace's event carries {kind: "repository", parent_slug: null, revoked_tokens: sorted string array, deleted_forks: sorted string array}
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/workspace/delete_test.go: with no fork remover registered, the stub token revoker returns ['t9', 't2'] for 'demo--a', [] for 'demo--b' and ['t5'] for 'demo'; DELETE 'demo'; read the parley.workspace.delete events in sequence order: assert three events with workspace 'demo--a', 'demo--b', 'demo'; assert the first has metadata {kind: 'fork', parent_slug: 'demo', revoked_tokens: ['t2', 't9']} and no deleted_forks member; the second has revoked_tokens []; the third has {kind: 'repository', parent_slug: null, revoked_tokens: ['t5'], deleted_forks: ['demo--a', 'demo--b']}; assert actor == caller on all; and a workspace without forks: one event with deleted_forks []; and with a stub fork remover whose RemoveForksOf returns ['demo--b', 'demo--a'] and writes no event: assert this package wrote exactly one event, for 'demo', with deleted_forks ['demo--a', 'demo--b']
   ```
1. [REQ-7.6] WHERE no sandbox remover, no token revoker, no remover of owned data, no fork remover, no session closer and no archive observer is registered, THE parleyd SHALL complete the archive and the delete by changing only the workspace records, the copy and the event log
   → archive answers HTTP 200 and delete HTTP 204; delete events carry revoked_tokens []
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/workspace/delete_test.go with an empty collaborator set: POST archive on a ready workspace with one fork: assert 200; DELETE it: assert 204, both rows gone, two parley.workspace.delete events with revoked_tokens []
   ```

### REQ-8: CLI commands for archive, reactivate, reclone and delete

**Rationale:** The owner retires, revives, repairs and removes a workspace from the shell, and cannot destroy data by a mistyped command.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-8.1] WHEN a user runs `parley workspace archive <slug>`, THE parley CLI SHALL send POST /workspaces/:slug/archive with a request timeout of 3 minutes and print the returned workspace
   → exit code 0; stdout is the workspace object as one JSON document
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/cli/workspace_test.go against an httptest server: run `parley workspace archive demo`; assert the server received POST /api/v1/workspaces/demo/archive with the Bearer credential and no body; assert stdout is the workspace JSON with status 'archived' and the exit code is 0; assert the command's request timeout is 3 minutes (a server that answers after 31 seconds on a fake clock still yields exit 0)
   ```
1. [REQ-8.2] WHEN a user runs `parley workspace reactivate <slug>` or `parley workspace reclone <slug> --confirm` without --wait, THE parley CLI SHALL send POST /workspaces/:slug/reactivate, or POST /workspaces/:slug/reclone with a request timeout of 3 minutes, and print the returned workspace
   → exit code 0; stdout is the workspace object with status "pending"
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/cli/workspace_test.go, table over {`workspace reactivate demo` -> POST /api/v1/workspaces/demo/reactivate, timeout 30 seconds; `workspace reclone demo --confirm` -> POST /api/v1/workspaces/demo/reclone, timeout 3 minutes}: assert method and path, no body; assert stdout is the returned workspace with status 'pending' and exit code 0; assert exactly one request was sent
   ```
1. [REQ-8.3] WHERE `parley workspace reactivate` or `parley workspace reclone` is run with --wait, THE parley CLI SHALL poll GET /workspaces/:slug after the route answered 200, every --poll-interval under --timeout, until the status is ready or failed, and print only the final workspace
   → ready: the final workspace on stdout, exit code 0; failed: the final workspace on stdout, error_type wait_failed on stderr, exit code 1; timeout: nothing on stdout, error_type wait_timeout on stderr, exit code 1
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/cli/workspace_test.go, table over {reactivate, reclone --confirm} x {server reports pending, cloning, then ready: stdout holds one document with status 'ready', exit 0; server reports failed: stdout holds the workspace with status 'failed', stderr holds an envelope with error_type 'wait_failed', exit 1; server stays pending with --timeout 50ms --poll-interval 10ms: stdout empty, stderr error_type 'wait_timeout', exit 1}: assert the first request is the POST and the later ones are GET /api/v1/workspaces/demo
   ```
1. [REQ-8.4] WHEN a user runs `parley workspace delete <slug> --confirm`, THE parley CLI SHALL send DELETE /workspaces/:slug and print a confirmation document that names the slug
   → exit code 0; stdout is {"status": "deleted", "slug": "<slug>"}; a hub error gives exit code 1 with the hub's envelope on stderr and nothing on stdout
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/cli/workspace_test.go: the httptest server answers 204 with no body; run `parley workspace delete demo --confirm`; assert the server received DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/demo; assert stdout parsed as JSON equals {status: 'deleted', slug: 'demo'}; assert exit code 0; and a row where the server answers 409 workspace_not_archived: assert stdout is empty, stderr holds that envelope, exit code 1
   ```
1. [REQ-8.5] IF `parley workspace reclone` or `parley workspace delete` is run without --confirm, THEN THE parley CLI SHALL stop before any request is sent and report a usage error
   → exit code 2; an error envelope with error_type usage_error on stderr; nothing on stdout; no HTTP request is sent
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/cli/workspace_test.go, table over {`workspace reclone demo`, `workspace reclone demo --wait`, `workspace delete demo`, `workspace delete demo --confirm=false`}: assert exit code 2; assert stderr holds an envelope with code 0 and error_type 'usage_error' whose message names --confirm; assert stdout is empty; assert the httptest server received no request
   ```

## Execution Paths

### PATH-1: A developer archives a workspace and reactivates it

1. **developer** runs `parley workspace archive demo`
2. **parley CLI** sends POST /api/v1/workspaces/demo/archive with a 3-minute timeout
3. **parleyd** sets the maintenance marker and offers every branch of its copy to origin as a fast-forward
4. **origin** accepts the branch main, which was ahead in the hub
5. **parleyd** sets status archived, writes parley.workspace.archive with origin_push ok, releases the marker and answers 200
6. **developer** runs `parley workspace reactivate demo --wait`
7. **parleyd** sets status pending, writes parley.workspace.reactivate and wakes the clone workers, which find the kept copy valid and set status ready
8. **parley CLI** polls GET /api/v1/workspaces/demo until status is ready and prints the workspace

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** parleyd started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0, the transactional store, internal/workspace handlers, safety copy and clone workers, internal/gitrepo with the git command, the parley CLI command tree, a test origin served over TLS by internal/gitrepo/gitrepotest

**Setup:**

- a developer with an API key registered the workspace demo from the test origin and it is ready
- a commit was added to main in the hub's copy that origin does not have
- the read route GET /workspaces/:slug of package 11 is mounted

**End state:**

- origin's main is at the commit that existed only in the hub
- after the archive command the stored status is archived and one parley.workspace.archive event with origin_push ok exists
- the reactivate command exits 0 and prints the workspace with status ready and the head_sha it had before the archive
- origin received no clone or fetch request between the reactivate and ready
- one parley.workspace.reactivate event exists

**Pseudocode:**

```
new test in test/e2e/workspace_retire_test.go: hub = startHub(t); origin = gitrepotest.Serve(t); create 'demo' and wait for ready; commit to main in the hub copy; out, code = cli('workspace', 'archive', 'demo'); assert code == 0 and out.status == 'archived'; assert origin.head('main') == hubCommit; n = origin.requestCount(); out, code = cli('workspace', 'reactivate', 'demo', '--wait', '--poll-interval', '50ms'); assert code == 0 and out.status == 'ready' and out.head_sha == hubCommit; assert origin.requestCount() == n; assert events('parley.workspace.archive') has 1 with origin_push 'ok'; assert events('parley.workspace.reactivate') has 1
```

### PATH-2: A developer deletes an archived workspace with a fork and registers the slug again

1. **developer** runs `parley workspace archive demo` and then `parley workspace delete demo --confirm`
2. **parley CLI** sends DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/demo
3. **parleyd** sets the maintenance marker and asks the sandbox remover to delete the sandboxes of demo and of its fork
4. **parleyd** in one transaction revokes bound tokens and runs the removers of owned data for the fork and for demo, removes both records and writes two parley.workspace.delete events
5. **parleyd** discards the repository data of demo, releases the marker and answers 204
6. **parley CLI** prints {"status": "deleted", "slug": "demo"} and exits 0
7. **developer** runs `parley workspace create --slug demo --git-url <origin>`
8. **parleyd** answers 201 with a new workspace in status pending and clones origin into a fresh copy

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** parleyd started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0, the transactional store and the event log, internal/workspace handlers and removal step, internal/gitrepo with the git command, the parley CLI command tree, a test origin served over TLS by internal/gitrepo/gitrepotest

**Setup:**

- the workspace demo is ready and has one fork record demo--t1, inserted through the store when the fork route of package 15 is not mounted
- a recording token revoker is registered in place of package 08's that returns the token id tok1 for demo--t1

**End state:**

- the delete command exits 0 and prints {status: deleted, slug: demo}
- no workspace record exists for demo or demo--t1 and the copy's directory is gone
- two parley.workspace.delete events exist: one for demo--t1 with kind fork and revoked_tokens [tok1], then one for demo with kind repository and deleted_forks [demo--t1]
- the events written for demo before the delete are still in the event log
- a new create with the slug demo answers 201 and the new workspace becomes ready with origin's branches only

**Pseudocode:**

```
new test in test/e2e/workspace_retire_test.go: hub = startHub(t, withTokenRevoker(rec)); create 'demo', wait ready; add fork row 'demo--t1'; push a branch local-only into the hub copy that origin refuses; cli('workspace', 'archive', 'demo'); out, code = cli('workspace', 'delete', 'demo', '--confirm'); assert code == 0 and out == {status: 'deleted', slug: 'demo'}; assert store has no row for 'demo' or 'demo--t1'; assert !exists(copyPath); ev = events('parley.workspace.delete'); assert len(ev) == 2 and ev[0].workspace == 'demo--t1' and ev[0].metadata.revoked_tokens == ['tok1'] and ev[1].metadata.deleted_forks == ['demo--t1']; assert events('parley.workspace.create', workspace 'demo') still has the first one; out, code = cli('workspace', 'create', '--slug', 'demo', '--git-url', origin.url, '--wait'); assert code == 0 and out.status == 'ready'; assert the new copy has no branch local-only
```

### PATH-3: A developer reclones a workspace from the shell

1. **developer** runs `parley workspace reclone demo --confirm --wait`
2. **parley CLI** sends POST /api/v1/workspaces/demo/reclone with a 3-minute timeout
3. **parleyd** sets the maintenance marker and offers every branch of its copy to origin as a fast-forward
4. **origin** accepts the branch feat and refuses the branch stale, which is not a fast-forward
5. **parleyd** sets status pending, clears sync_error and the origin heads, writes parley.workspace.reclone with origin_push partial, discards its copy and answers 200
6. **parleyd** clones origin into a fresh copy and sets status ready
7. **parley CLI** polls GET /api/v1/workspaces/demo until status is ready, prints the workspace and exits 0

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** parleyd started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0, the transactional store, internal/workspace handlers, safety copy and clone workers, internal/gitrepo with the git command, the parley CLI command tree, a test origin served over TLS by internal/gitrepo/gitrepotest

**Setup:**

- the workspace demo is ready, cloned from the test origin, which has branches main and stale
- in the hub's copy a branch feat exists that origin lacks and stale was rewritten so that origin refuses it
- the read route GET /workspaces/:slug of package 11 is mounted

**End state:**

- the command exits 0 and prints the workspace with status ready
- origin has feat at the hub's former commit and stale at its own old commit
- the hub's new copy has stale at origin's commit and feat at the accepted commit
- one parley.workspace.reclone event with origin_push partial exists
- running the command without --confirm exits 2 and origin and the hub receive no request

**Pseudocode:**

```
new test in test/e2e/workspace_retire_test.go: hub, origin as above; create 'demo', wait ready; add feat and rewrite stale in the hub copy; _, code = cli('workspace', 'reclone', 'demo'); assert code == 2 and hub.requestCount unchanged; out, code = cli('workspace', 'reclone', 'demo', '--confirm', '--wait', '--poll-interval', '50ms'); assert code == 0 and out.status == 'ready'; assert origin.head('feat') == featCommit and origin.head('stale') == originStale; assert hubCopy.head('stale') == originStale; assert events('parley.workspace.reclone')[0].metadata.origin_push == 'partial'
```

## Test Commands

- **all_tests:** `go test ./... -count=1`
- **linter:** `golangci-lint run ./...`
- **spec_tests:** `go test ./internal/workspace/... ./internal/gitrepo/... ./internal/cli/... ./test/e2e/... -count=1`

## Dependencies

- `08` — wires RevokeBoundTo of that package as the token revoker of the removal step, so that the delete events name the revoked tokens
- `09` — builds its CLI commands on the client, output and exit-code helpers of the CLI foundation
- `10` — uses the workspace record, the state guard's maintenance marker, the clone-work entry point, origin credential resolution and the copy operations of internal/gitrepo that package 10 delivers
- `11` — waits and smoke checks read the workspace through GET /workspaces/:slug
- `13` — uses the push mode of the test origin (SmartOrigin) with its switches to refuse an update and to stall, which that package adds to internal/gitrepo/gitrepotest
- `52` — emits its hub events through the event log component

### 1. Offer every branch to origin as a fast-forward safety copy (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-2.1, REQ-2.2, REQ-2.3, REQ-2.4

**Steps:**

- 1.2 In internal/gitrepo add an operation that pushes a given list of branches of a bare copy to the same-named branches of a remote URL in one git subprocess, without force, without tags and without deletions, with the credential passed the way package 10 passes it to git, and that returns one result for each branch: pushed, up to date or rejected
- 1.3 Make the operation honour its context: when the context ends, the git subprocess is stopped and the results gathered so far are returned
- 1.4 In internal/workspace add the safety copy: list the branches under refs/heads/ of the workspace's copy, drop the integration branch when workspace_mode is carry_patch, resolve the origin credential from the workspace's secrets through package 10's resolver, and call the push operation under a 2-minute deadline that tests can shorten
- 1.5 When the workspace has no copy on disk (status failed), offer nothing and report ok without calling git

- 1.8 For every accepted branch, set refs/remotes/origin/<name> of the hub's copy to the pushed commit with SetOriginHead of internal/gitrepo (package 10); leave the origin heads of refused branches as they are
- 1.9 Return the outcome and never an error to the caller; log a failure with the slug after passing the text through the hub's scrubber

### 2. Archive a repository workspace (implement)

### 3. End sessions and notify observers when a workspace is archived (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-3.6, REQ-3.7, REQ-3.8

**Depends on:** 2

**Steps:**

- 3.1 Add the session and observer behaviours to internal/workspace/archive_test.go and confirm they fail
- 3.2 In internal/workspace/teardown.go define the collaborators other packages supply, as one set (Teardown) that the hub's composition fills at start and of which an empty one is valid: SandboxRemover (takes the slugs), TokenRevoker (takes the transaction and slugs and returns the ids of the tokens it revoked), Remover of owned data (takes the transaction and one slug and returns an error), SessionCloser (takes the transaction, the slugs and a reason), ArchiveObserver (takes the slug and the fork slugs) and ForkRemover
- 3.3 Declare ForkRemover as the one interface between this package and package 16, with two methods: DeleteFork(ctx, slug, caller), which serves DELETE for a fork and returns nil or an API error, and RemoveForksOf(ctx, transaction, parent slug, actor), which removes every fork of a parent inside the parent's delete transaction, writes each fork's parley.workspace.delete event and returns the removed slugs and a function that discards the forks' repository data after the commit
- 3.4 Export RemoveOwned(ctx, transaction, slug, reason): it calls the token revoker for the slug, every remover of owned data in registration order and the session closer with the slug and the reason, and returns the revoked token ids sorted ascending; the removal step of this package and the fork removal of package 16 both remove a workspace's owned data through it and through nothing else

- 3.8 Call no observer and no closer when the archive is refused

### 5. Reclone a repository workspace (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-5

**Depends on:** 2

**Steps:**

- 5.1 Add the reclone behaviours to internal/workspace/reclone_test.go and confirm they fail
- 5.2 Register POST /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/reclone with the scope workspaces:write and write access; ignore any request body
- 5.3 Refuse in this order: a fork with 400 fork_has_no_origin; a set marker with 409 workspace_busy; status archived with 409 workspace_archived; status pending or cloning with 409 workspace_busy; at least one fork record with 409 has_forks
- 5.4 With the marker held, run the safety copy
- 5.5 In one transaction set status pending, clear sync_error and origin_head_sha, replace the record's instance id (package 10 compares it when it checks an existing copy), and write parley.workspace.reclone with metadata origin_push; leave head_sha, default_branch and last_sync_at as they are
- 5.6 When the transaction fails answer 500 internal and leave the record and the copy as they were
- 5.7 After the commit remove the copy from disk through internal/gitrepo, which removes the origin heads (refs/remotes/origin/*) with it, then wake the clone workers through package 10's entry point; keep the removal step replaceable in tests, so that a stop between commit and removal can be reproduced
- 5.8 Answer 200 with the workspace response object; detach the work from the request's cancellation once the checks have passed
- 5.9 Call no remover of owned data: change records and every other package's data stay

**Touches:**

- `internal/workspace/reclone.go`
- `internal/workspace/reclone_test.go`

### 6. Delete an archived workspace with its forks in one step (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-6.1, REQ-6.2, REQ-6.5, REQ-6.6, REQ-6.7, REQ-7

**Depends on:** 3

**Steps:**

- 6.1 Add the delete behaviours to internal/workspace/delete_test.go and confirm they fail; the tests register stub collaborators that record their calls and write test rows through the transaction they are given
- 6.2 Register DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{slug} with the scope workspaces:write and write access
- 6.3 For a repository workspace refuse a set marker with 409 workspace_busy and any status other than archived with 409 workspace_not_archived
- 6.4 With the marker held, collect the slugs of the forks in ascending order and call the sandbox remover with the workspace's slug and theirs; on its error answer 500 internal and change nothing
- 6.5 Run the removal step as one store transaction: when a fork remover is registered call its RemoveForksOf with the transaction, the workspace's slug and the caller, and keep the slugs and the discard function it returns; otherwise, for each fork in ascending slug order, call RemoveOwned with the reason `workspace deleted`, delete the fork's record with its settings and write its event; then do the same three things for the workspace itself
- 6.6 Fill each parley.workspace.delete event this package writes with kind, parent_slug and revoked_tokens (the ids RemoveOwned returned for that slug, an empty list when none), and the workspace's event, written last, also with deleted_forks: the fork slugs sorted ascending, taken from RemoveForksOf when a fork remover is registered
- 6.7 On any error inside the step roll the transaction back, answer 500 internal and leave the repository data in place
- 6.8 After the commit discard the workspace's repository data through internal/gitrepo and call the discard function a fork remover returned; never call it after a rollback; log a failure with the slug and the path and still answer 204
- 6.9 Answer 204 with an empty body; delete no row of the event log or of the audit store
- 6.10 Detach the work from the request's cancellation once the checks have passed

**Touches:**

- `internal/workspace/delete.go`
- `internal/workspace/delete_test.go`
- `internal/workspace/teardown.go`

**Done when:**

- the checks of the criteria listed above exist as tests, are executable and pass
- `go test ./... -count=1` passes
- `golangci-lint run ./...` passes

### 7. Hold exclusive maintenance and the access rules across the four routes (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-1, REQ-6.3, REQ-6.4

- 7.6 Check on all four routes that an organization member gets 403 forbidden whatever the status, a caller with no access and an unknown slug get the same 404 not_found, a token without workspaces:write gets 403 insufficient_scope, and that none of these contacts origin or a collaborator
- 7.7 Check for archive, reclone and delete that a request whose context is cancelled after the checks still ends in the same stored state as a connected one
